bridge_statement: If one deterministic algorithm decides every 3-CNF instance in polynomial time by exact answer-blind dispatch, exact representation-preserving transitions, polynomially bounded charged work, and polynomially bounded termination, then 3SAT is in P; by NP-completeness of 3SAT, P=NP.

algorithm_contract.input: arbitrary 3-CNF F of encoded size N
algorithm_contract.allowed_step: either certified polynomial terminal decision or exact certified transition F -> F'
forbidden: unbounded brute-force fallback with decision authority
post-hoc route selection using ground truth

premises.statement: For every 3-CNF F, the dispatcher either returns a certified terminal decision or an admissible exact successor; it never remains permanently OPEN.
Every admitted transition preserves satisfiability exactly: SAT(F) iff SAT(F'). Every terminal decision carries an independently checkable certificate or exact tractable decision proof.

There exists a fixed constant c such that discovery, compilation, verification, and terminal work for each step are bounded by N^c in the original input size N, including bit complexity and serialized proof material.
Every reachable representation/state has encoded size at most N^c for one fixed c independent of the input instance and trajectory.
There exists a polynomially bounded well-founded rank Phi such that every nonterminal admitted transition strictly decreases Phi, hence the number of transitions is polynomial in N.
The complete returned SAT witness or UNSAT derivation can be independently replayed against the original input in polynomial time.

derivation: U1 gives total coverage of arbitrary 3-CNF.
U2 prevents semantic corruption across representation switches.
U3 and U4 bound each charged stage by a polynomial in original input size.
U5 bounds the number of stages by a polynomial in original input size.
Therefore the composed deterministic algorithm decides 3SAT in polynomial time.
3SAT is NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
Hence every language in NP reduces in polynomial time to 3SAT and is decidable in polynomial time.
Thus NP subseteq P; since P subseteq NP, P = NP.
